unspecified_scores.reason: Every addon proxy request reaches db.close() at backend/app/routers/addon_proxy.py:613, but on routes that never queried, Session.close() on a session with no checked-out connection is a no-op, and get_db's second close at backend/app/database.py:708 is idempotent, so the user sees nothing.

specification_compliance: addon_proxy.py:613 closes the request Session after every gate (drive scope, pre_check, addon_feature) and before _proxy_request, which matches the stated intent of not pinning a pooled connection while waiting on upstream.

No DB use follows the close: _proxy_request takes no db, and _accessible_drives (addon_proxy.py:45-49) and _apply_drive_access_filter read config, not the Session. get_unlocked_groups (auth.py:144) does not depend on get_db.
file_access's checked_drive is read from file.drive at addon_proxy.py:568-570, before the close, so no detached-instance lazy load happens later.
regression_risks: Any future code added after addon_proxy.py:613 that uses `db` would silently open a new connection (SQLAlchemy Session reuse after close) and pin it again; or, if it touches an ORM instance loaded before the close, it would hit a DetachedInstanceError. Nothing in the code prevents this except the comment.
test_coverage: backend/tests/test_addon_proxy_releases_db.py exists and targets the connection-release behavior with a fake slow upstream (aclose stubs at lines 69 and 85); I did not read its assertions in full or run it.
